polyvios.name: Polyvios
tags: Weekday evening, an open portion off the charcoal
polyvios.why: Polyvios Silvestridis was driven out of Pontic Ordu — Kotyora — in the 1922 uprooting; in 1935 he opened the oldest of Drapetsona's Agiou Dimitriou kebab row, first as a cookhouse feeding the new quarter the flavours of home. His grandson, another Polyvios, keeps it exactly as it was: everything cut and made by hand, the meat from the neighbourhood's own shops, and a soutzouki made 'the way the Pontic grandfather made it' — a recipe he gives to no one. Of the row's old houses — Dimakis, Savvas, Karababas, Avraam, Polyvios — only three still burn charcoal.
polyvios.verdict: Drapetsona's oldest kebab house — a Pontic refugee's 1935 grill, still hand-cutting every portion three generations on, on a kebab row that has all but gone cold around it.
polyvios.signature: Merida (open portion): two pitas heaped with charcoal meat, quartered tomato, onion and parsley.
polyvios.caveat: Not central and not a scene — a back-street Drapetsona grill beyond the port gates, charcoal-and-meat only, cash; phone ahead.
polyvios.person: Founded 1935 by Polyvios Silvestridis, a Pontic Greek refugee from Ordu (Kotyora); run today by his grandson, also Polyvios, who makes everything by hand and guards the family soutzouki recipe.

alargino.name: Alargino
alargino.neighborhood: Nikaia · Agiou Ioannou, near the centre
tags: A music night, for old-Kokkinia atmosphere
alargino.why: Alargino sells the memory of old Kokkinia as much as its food. It occupies a 1938 building on Agiou Ioannou in Nikaia, at the edge of the old refugee quarter, and the plates that vanish fastest are the handmade Smyrnaïka soutzoukakia and the pastourmalopita — the Anatolian pantry the 1922 refugees carried west. On weekend nights live strings turn the room into a small refugee-quarter kompania. The menu widens to Epirot pan-fried pork and Cretan snail stifado, but the Smyrna backbone is the reason In2life named it among the best mezedes of Nikaia.
alargino.verdict: The neighbourhood table that keeps Smyrna on the plate — handmade Smyrnaïka soutzoukakia and pastourma pie under live strings.
alargino.signature: Smyrnaïka soutzoukakia: handmade cumin-scented mince in tomato, the refugee city on a plate.
alargino.caveat: Not a quiet or gourmet room — a loud, music-filled neighbourhood mezedopoleio, not a destination showpiece.

taverna-tou-katsogiannou.name: Taverna tou Katsogiannou
taverna-tou-katsogiannou.neighborhood: Drapetsona · opposite the church of Agios Panteleimon
tags: Lunch, for the magirefta and meatballs
taverna-tou-katsogiannou.why: Grigoris Katsogiannis opened it in 1930 as a dairy shop, then began grilling cod and chops over charcoal — which makes it the oldest taverna in Drapetsona. Since 2005 Dora (Theodora) Stavridou has run it, cooking about six daily-changing magirefta from family recipes and hand-cutting the fries herself. The room is a working time-capsule of refugee Drapetsona: a mirrored 1930 wooden refrigerator — a British Prestcold — still stands and still runs, opposite the church of Agios Panteleimon. Lunch is the hour; the six rotating pot-dishes and the hand-cut fries are the quiet draw, closed Sunday evenings and Mondays.
taverna-tou-katsogiannou.hours: Lunch daily; closed Mon & Sun evenings
taverna-tou-katsogiannou.verdict: The oldest taverna in Drapetsona (since 1930), where Dora Stavridou's ouzo-doused meatballs in red sauce have become, in the local phrase, 'an urban myth.'
taverna-tou-katsogiannou.signature: Keftedakia me ouzo: ouzo-flambéed meatballs in red sauce, hand-cut fries for dipping.
taverna-tou-katsogiannou.caveat: Not for late-night eating or a big fish spread — lunch-focused, closed Sunday evenings and Mondays, firmly meat-and-magirefta.
taverna-tou-katsogiannou.person: Opened 1930 as a dairy shop by Grigoris Katsogiannis; since 2005 run by Dora (Theodora) Stavridou, who cooks about six daily-changing dishes from family recipes and hand-cuts the fries.

vosporos.name: Vosporos
tags: Dinner, a night with live politika/smyrneika
vosporos.why: 'Politiki kouzina' is the cooking the Greeks of Constantinople and Asia Minor carried west — the heritage that filled Kokkinia, Nikaia and Drapetsona with refugees after 1922. Vosporos has kept those Bosphorus flavours on the Mikrolimano quay for twenty-two years: halloumi fried squeaky-hot, adana kebab with yogurt, hunkar begendi over smoky eggplant, the cured pastourma and soutzouki of the Bosphorus. Some nights the room turns over to live politika and smyrneika song. It sits three coves from the fish-taverna touts and cooks nothing Aegean — meat and mezze, in Constantinople measure.
vosporos.verdict: Piraeus's one genuine Politiki-cuisine table — Bosphorus meat-and-mezze in outsized portions, where a Piraeus chef sends you when she wants everything but fish.
vosporos.signature: Oversized peinirli: a boat of molten four-cheese and pastourma, straight from the oven.
vosporos.caveat: Not for small appetites or fish-taverna seekers — meat- and mezze-heavy Politiki cooking in enormous portions, not Aegean seafood.

toukta-thai-food.name: Toukta Thai Food
toukta-thai-food.neighborhood: Nikaia · Ionias & Thrakis, the 1922 refugee grid
tags: Book ahead; the tiny room fills fast
toukta-thai-food.why: In a grid of low refugee houses whose grills still cook Smyrna and Pontos, a Thai kitchen the size of a living room quietly extends the neighbourhood's immigrant story a century after the 1922 refugees laid it out. Uthaiwan Wannasuk pounds her own curry pastes and folds fresh curry and noodles for six tables at a time, on the corner of Ionias and Thrakis in Nikaia. FlagInLife called it 'an unexpected Thai experience'; there is no Greek-classics menu and no room for a big group — you book, or you don't get in.
toukta-thai-food.verdict: Proof Kokkinia's immigrant table didn't end in 1922 — a six-table Thai kitchen turning out the real, fresh-pounded thing at €7 a plate.
toukta-thai-food.signature: Pad thai: tamarind-slicked rice noodles, peanuts, lime, wok-hot and fresh.
toukta-thai-food.caveat: Not for the taverna-traditionalist or big groups — a cramped six-table room with no Greek-classics menu.
toukta-thai-food.person: Owner-cook Uthaiwan Wannasuk, who pounds her own curry pastes and folds fresh pad thai for six tables at a time.

sushi-rolls.name: Sushi Rolls
sushi-rolls.neighborhood: Piraeus centre · behind Agios Nikolaos, near Akti Miaouli
tags: Weekday evening, when the offices empty
sushi-rolls.why: For about a decade a small sushi bar has worked a quiet side street behind the church of Agios Nikolaos, patron of sailors, near Akti Miaouli — the office street of Greek shipping. By day the room doubles as the canteen of the surrounding shipping companies: Japanese fish, cut to order, for the people who move ships. The fish comes from Greek suppliers and the menu is refreshed yearly. Athens Voice called it 'a diamond of Japanese cuisine in Piraeus' in 2025 — a real find, if an honest one: solid, not a 50 Best or Michelin headline.
sushi-rolls.verdict: The reliable non-Greek table with a story — a shipping-office-canteen sushi bar behind the seamen's church, cut to order for the people who move ships.
sushi-rolls.signature: Crispy Salmon & Tuna Garlic rolls: cut to order, with cold or warm sake.
sushi-rolls.caveat: Not a headline — Piraeus's real 'foreign' greatness is the refugee kitchen; this is the reliable, honest table with a story.

o-giorgos.name: O Giorgos
o-giorgos.neighborhood: Central Piraeus · Gounari, by the old flea market
tags: Weekday lunch, straight off the grill
o-giorgos.why: Grigoris Tsakiris and his son Giorgos set up in 2019 in the old flea-market lanes behind the fish market, wanting to make souvlaki 'as it used to be' — plain, hand-formed, no gimmicks. A small cult formed fast: in2life ranked it first of Piraeus's top five souvlaki in May 2025, and Cookout/SKAI made it the first stop on its port crawl that July. The pita is their own recipe and the spicy red sauce house-made, and nothing is padded with fries. It runs daytime only, closes by early evening, and the queue is part of the deal.
o-giorgos.verdict: Piraeus's cult modern souvlaki — a ~€2.50 hand-formed beef-meatball wrap that locals and the food press repeatedly rank the city's best.
o-giorgos.signature: Bifteki wrap: two hand-formed beef meatballs, salt and pepper, soft pita, spicy red sauce.
o-giorgos.caveat: Not for a sit-down dinner — daytime only, closes early evening, seating barely there.

souvlakia-o-serkos.name: Souvlakia o Serkos
tags: Early evening, when the plateia fills
souvlakia-o-serkos.why: Sarkis 'Serkos' Hanikyan reached Kokkinia with the Armenians who survived the fire of Smyrna and the genocide; he first sold dried nuts off a cart near the Esperos cinema, then learned to grind and grill kebab, opening around 1972. Two generations on, his daughter Agavni ('Anni') works the charcoal and his son Evendis runs the shop, and the kitchen keeps its one dogma — good meat, salt, pepper, fire, nothing else: 'this kebab doesn't burden anyone.' The tables sit out on Plateia Neraidas, in the old refugee quarter Kokkinia became after 1922.
souvlakia-o-serkos.hours: Midday into evening; call to confirm
souvlakia-o-serkos.verdict: Piraeus's last Armenian charcoal kebab — a refugee family's salt-and-pepper mince that shames every over-spiced imitation.
souvlakia-o-serkos.signature: Armenian kebab: lamb-and-beef mince, only salt and pepper, charcoal-blistered, pillow-soft.
souvlakia-o-serkos.caveat: Not for spice-seekers or a polished dinner — a plateia grill shack, a handful of items, cash.
souvlakia-o-serkos.person: Opened by Sarkis 'Serkos' Hanikyan, an Armenian who began as a street nut-vendor before mastering the kebab (LiFO gives 1972); today his daughter Agavni ('Anni') works the charcoal and his son Evendis runs the shop.

o-karabelas.name: O Karabelas
o-karabelas.neighborhood: Neo Faliro edge · Pylis, near Karaiskakis Stadium
tags: Early evening, before the gyro sells out
o-karabelas.why: The walls are a working museum to Olympiacos — scarves, photographs, pennants floor to ceiling — so you eat inside a red-and-white shrine a short walk from the club's Karaiskakis ground. Spiros and Eleni have wrapped souvlaki here for about thirty of the shop's near-fifty years; Eleni Barkolia is the registered proprietor and makes the slightly spicy red sauce that regulars come for. It opens at six in the evening, closes Sundays, and there is no comfortable place to sit. in2life keeps it on the Piraeus top-five, and the gyro sometimes sells out before the night is old.
o-karabelas.verdict: The most atmospheric old-school souvlatzidiko in Piraeus — half Olympiacos museum, half standing-room grill, still turning out ~€3 wraps after nearly fifty years.

o-karabelas.caveat: Not for a comfortable meal or the sauce-shy — a cramped, standing-room grill, evenings only.
o-karabelas.person: Run for roughly three decades by Spiros and Eleni (Eleni Barkolia is the registered proprietor); walls packed floor-to-ceiling with Olympiacos memorabilia, a short walk from the club's Karaiskakis ground.

mastronikolas.name: Mastronikolas
tags: Mid-morning, a warm slice with Greek coffee
mastronikolas.why: The Mastronikolas grandfather began by delivering milk around the Profitis Ilias neighbourhood by donkey in 1909; the family still keeps his original tin milk-can as an heirloom. Panagiotis, the third-generation owner, has just had a son to make the fourth generation on the same corner. After the shop turned up, unbidden, in a French Petit Futé guide, customers began driving in from Thessaloniki and Crete — even Sweden and France — for a warm slab from the counter. It is a place to take away from, not to linger at; there is no savoury breakfast, only sweets and made-in-house kaimaki ice cream.
mastronikolas.verdict: The oldest galaktopoleio in Piraeus (since 1909), whose generous, crisp-topped galaktoboureko ranks among the best in Attica.
mastronikolas.signature: Galaktoboureko: warm, semolina custard oozing under shatter-crisp golden phyllo.
mastronikolas.caveat: Not a place to linger — a sweets counter to take away, with no savoury or brunch breakfast.

euxeinon.name: Euxeinon
euxeinon.neighborhood: Trouba · Navarchou Notara, by the port
tags: Mid-morning, when the fryer is going
euxeinon.why: Parthenope (Partheni) Amanitidou fled Trebizond, on the Black Sea, in 1922, carrying her family's piroski recipe; only in 1977 did she open her own tiny shop near the ferry gates. The name means 'of the Euxine — the Black Sea,' the Pontos the family came from. Her son Spyros, a former captain, starts the dough around three in the morning; his wife Vasiliki and grandsons Giorgos and Haris work the counter. The fillings use Tripoli barrel-aged feta, Mytilene kaseri and Naxos potatoes. Fried, hearty and gone by midday — LiFO put it among the port's best piroski in 2022.
euxeinon.hours: Mornings from ~03:00 bake until the midday sellout
euxeinon.verdict: The best-loved piroski in Piraeus — a half-century Pontic-refugee bakery frying cheese and mince pockets golden to order from an unbroken family recipe.
euxeinon.signature: Piroski kima: golden, blistered mince pocket, fried to order and eaten scalding.
euxeinon.caveat: Fried, hearty and gone by midday — not for a light, sweet or late breakfast; a grab-and-go counter.

bougatsa-pavlidi.name: Bougatsa Pavlidi
bougatsa-pavlidi.neighborhood: Nikaia · Petrou Ralli, near the state hospital
tags: 3–6 a.m., phyllo hot off the tray
bougatsa-pavlidi.why: When his brother-in-law lost his mill job, Leonidas Pavlidis learned to pull phyllo from a Pomak baker in Sapes, in Rhodope, and opened on an unpaved Petrou Ralli in 1974. Through the 1970s to 90s artists came at three in the morning for sweet bougatsa rather than the tripe-soup shops. His daughter Sophia Dridaki-Pavlidi runs it now, with her son Giorgos learning the trade; she says her father's version simply 'made the difference somehow.' The family still bakes fresh before dawn, deep in residential Nikaia — a bus or taxi from the harbour, no seats, no coffee ritual.
bougatsa-pavlidi.hours: Open 24 hours; fresh bake before dawn
bougatsa-pavlidi.verdict: The last 24-hour phyllo workshop in working-class Piraeus, still turning out the port's benchmark bougatsa fresh before dawn.
bougatsa-pavlidi.signature: Sweet bougatsa: crackling hot phyllo, warm semolina cream, caramelised sugar, cinnamon dust.
bougatsa-pavlidi.caveat: Not a café — no seats, no coffee ritual, no view; a bakery counter deep in residential Nikaia, a bus or taxi from the harbour.

tags: € · a couple of euros a kalamaki

kantina-o-plastiras.why: Wedged among trucks and the derelict conveyor that once loaded fertilizer onto ships from the Lipasmata works, the canteen's walls are papered with photographs of General Nikolaos Plastiras. The owner, surname Fortetsanakis, runs it with his wife Anna; chef Vasilis Kallidis filmed here for LiFO. One regular told the crew he lives up in Alexandras and takes a taxi all the way down 'to eat the best souvlaki in the city and go home.' Forty years on the same raw Drapetsona quay, and the hours are whatever the port needs — early, and long after the night out.
